reference.title: Band Seated Twist
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you turn away from the anchor, breathe in as you come back.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s away, short pause, 1.5 s back

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of losing the tall seated posture (clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: sit farther from the anchor for more tension
prescription.progression: Stronger band, longer pause at the end, feet lifted

cues.text: Sit side-on to the anchor, knees bent, feet flat, trunk tall and leaning back slightly. Hold the band handle in both hands, arms long in front of the chest, band at chest height.
Breathe out and turn the ribs and shoulders away from the anchor; the hands stay in front of the breastbone.
Pause at the end; hips and knees stay still, chest lifted.
Turn back slowly toward the anchor, controlling the band.
Short pause just past the middle, then turn again. Turn around to train the other side.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the arms while the trunk stays still
mistakes.fix: Keep the hands in front of the breastbone and turn the ribs and shoulders.

mistakes.mistake: Slumping into a rounded low back
mistakes.fix: Sit tall; lean back less or sit on a folded mat.
Keep the knees together and the pelvis still.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap you back

kinematics.norm: Moderate range, mostly thoracic; end-range twisting under flexion is the concern (Marshall and McGill 2010)
Tall, leaning back a little (clinical opinion)
Together in front of the chest, arms long, turning with the trunk (clinical opinion)
Knees bent, feet flat, pelvis still (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band Seated Twist, video (movement reference)
Torso-twist exercise with elastic resistance vs a training machine: core muscle EMG (Scientifica 2015:403068; PubMed 26557405)
Oliva-Lozano and Muyor 2020, core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306)
Marshall and McGill 2010, the role of axial torque in disc herniation (Clin Biomech 25:6-9), porcine model

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Check the band and the anchor before each set: a band that slips or snaps can hit you.
Repeated twisting combined with flexion promoted disc injury in a porcine model (Marshall and McGill 2010): sit tall and keep the range moderate.
Disc herniation, rotation intolerance, osteoporosis: use an anti-rotation hold (Pallof press) instead.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: sit on a folded mat or a low box and make the turn smaller.
Hip flexors cramp: lean back less.
regressions: Lighter band or sit closer to the anchor.

muscleNotes.obliques_r: Turn the trunk against the band: the external oblique of one side works with the internal oblique of the other. In elastic-band torso twists the external oblique reached about 54-77% MVC (Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Turn the trunk against the band (oblique pair across the trunk; Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus and transversus abdominis hold the leaned-back sit (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the chest lifted and help the rotation (erector spinae about 32-50% MVC in torso twists, Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the chest lifted and help the rotation (Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Hold the hips flexed so the trunk does not fall back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Hold the hips flexed so the trunk does not fall back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Hold the arms out in front (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Hold the arms out in front (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.pec_r: Keep the hands together in front of the chest (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Keep the hands together in front of the chest (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades set as the band pulls (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades set as the band pulls (clinical opinion).
